channel.title: The 13 Principles of Faith — Dayan Daniel Kada
channel.description: Dayan Daniel Kada's two courses on the Rambam's 13 Principles of Faith: Sunday nights in Wembley (2018-19) and Tuesday nights at Tiferet Eyal (2019-20).
channel.itunes:author: Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: Why Does Judaism Need Principles of Faith? | The 13 Principles of Faith, Introduction
item.description:
Why did the Rambam turn belief into a system? The introduction presents him as halakhist, philosopher, commentator and physician, and the first to set out Jewish belief systematically. It explains the three groups of the 13 principles, why they must be known, and the meaning of emunah.

item.description:
The first principle: what does it mean that there is a Creator? God as perfect, self-sufficient, necessary and the source of all, and why logical impossibility is no flaw. The class weighs the first-cause and design arguments and the role of feeling in emunah.

item.title: The Uniqueness of the Unity of God | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 2
item.description:
Principle two says that God is one in a way unlike any other oneness. The class shows how Hashem Ehad rules out polytheism, dualism, the Trinity, deism and pantheism, discusses subtle everyday dualism, Hakham David Nieto, and why God has no parts or positive attributes.

item.title: No Body, No Form: The Hardest Principle to Accept? | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 3
item.description:
Why does the Rambam rule out any body or form for God? Principle 3: bodily descriptions in Tanakh are metaphors, the Raavad and most Rishonim disagree with the Rambam on the naive believer, and the Rabbi agrees with them. Teach children early.

item.title: Was the World Made from Nothing? | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 4
item.description:

item.title: Why Pray If God Needs Nothing? | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 5
item.description:
If God needs nothing, what is prayer for? Principle 5: serve God, serve nothing else, and serve Him through nothing else. Three ways to understand prayer, none of which changes God's mind, and how idolatry began and where honouring intermediaries, including angels, crosses the line.

item.title: What Made Moshe's Prophecy Different? | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 7
item.description:
Could any prophet ever equal Moshe? The seventh principle describes prophecy without an intermediary, while awake, without fear and at will. Other prophets saw through dull lenses, but the Torah came through a clear lens. The Rambam holds that no one will equal Moshe, while the Ramban and Albo disagree.

item.title: If God Knows What I Will Do, Am I Free? | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 10
item.description:
How can God know what we will do and still leave us free? Principle 10 on providence, free will as a principle of faith, the answers of Saadiah Gaon, the Ralbag and Crescas, and the Rambam, who holds both because God's knowledge is beyond ours.

item.title: Reward and Punishment Are the Person You Become | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 11

item.title: Mashiah: A Person, an Era, or Both? | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 12
item.description:
What exactly must a Jew believe about Mashiah? The twelfth principle is to believe in him and await him, without calculating when he will come. The Rambam insists on a personal king from David's line who needs no miracles, in a messianic age that is still the natural world with free will.

item.title: Body or Soul? The Rambam on the Resurrection | The 13 Principles of Faith, Principle 13
item.description:
